title: Tak 3 Days 2 Nights 2026 — Town, Mae Sot & Nature Plan | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An easy 3-day, 2-night Tak itinerary in Thailand: start in the old town at Trok Ban Chin, cross the mountains to Mae Sot, hit Rim Moei border market and Wat Thai Wattanaram, then finish at Pha Charoen Waterfall — with real times, distances and rough costs.
keywords: Tak 3 days 2 nights, Tak itinerary, Mae Sot travel, Trok Ban Chin, Rim Moei market, Pha Charoen Waterfall
h1:
Tak in 3 Days 2 Nights
Town · Mae Sot · Nature
intro: Tak is a big province with two very different moods in one place. The town side sits quietly along the Ping River with old-quarter charm, while across the mountains lies Mae Sot, a border town where Thai and Burmese cultures blend into something all its own. This 3-day, 2-night plan keeps the driving smooth with no backtracking: start in Tak town, cross the mountains to sleep in Mae Sot, then wrap up with some nature before heading home.

blocks.html: It's roughly 73–86 km from Tak town to Mae Sot, following Highways 105/12 over the mountains past Doi Phawo, about an hour and a half of driving. Sequence it well and you can stop at sights along the way without racing through the mountains after dark. This plan suits anyone with their own car or a rental, since the sights are spread out and public transport between them is limited.

items: Day 1 — Tak town: Trok Ban Chin, Wat Sitalaram, the Rattanakosin Bicentennial Suspension Bridge, overnight in town
Day 2 — Cross the mountains to Mae Sot: Wat Thai Wattanaram, the Rim Moei border market, overnight in Mae Sot
Day 3 — Nature before you leave: Pha Charoen Waterfall, a soak in the hot springs, then back to Tak town

blocks.title: Sort Out the Car First
blocks.html: If you fly into Mae Sot airport you can flip the order — start in Mae Sot and drive into Tak town on the last day. But if you're coming by bus or driving from Bangkok, hitting Tak town first as this plan does is smoother, since you won't have to cross the mountains there and back twice.

items.label: Day trips from Tak
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Tak Town on the Ping River

items.activity: Walk Trok Ban Chin, Taksin Road, Rahaeng subdistrict
items.note: A century-old Chinese community where dozens of wooden houses built by Chinese merchant immigrants line the lane. It's an easy, relaxed walk for photos, with cafes and dessert shops tucked along the way.
Right near Trok Ban Chin, with an old wooden viharn in a mixed style — you can walk straight over from the lane, no need to drive.

items.activity: Lunch in town plus a cafe break
items.note: Tak town has several garden-style wooden-house cafes, such as Thiang Na Coffee and Bakery Farm near Phahonyothin Road — a good spot to rest out of the afternoon sun.
A suspension bridge about 700 m long crossing the Ping River. Walk across for the sunset, and after dark it's lit up — one of Tak's best-known photo spots.

items.activity: Dinner by the Ping River, then check in to your hotel in town
items.note: Staying in Tak town on the first night makes it easy to grab riverside food and to head out early the next morning.

blocks.title: Day-One Tip
blocks.html: Trok Ban Chin is livelier on weekends than on weekdays. If you want the full market-and-street-food atmosphere, try to line up your first day with a Saturday or Sunday.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Over the Mountains to the Mae Sot Border

items.activity: Leave Tak town, drive Highways 105/12 over Doi Phawo
items.note: About 73–86 km, roughly an hour and a half. It's a winding mountain road, so drive slowly and watch for trucks — there are viewpoints to pull over and rest along the way.

items.activity: Reach Mae Sot, stop at Wat Thai Wattanaram
items.note: A century-old Tai-style temple in Burmese architecture in Tha Sai Luat subdistrict, known for its golden viharn, Mon-style chedi and the pair of golden lions out front — plenty of Burmese architecture to take in.

items.activity: Burmese and Shan food in Mae Sot town
items.note: Mae Sot has plenty of Burmese dishes to try, from khao man som tam to mohinga and Burmese-side sweets, all at easy prices.

items.activity: Rim Moei market on the Thai-Myanmar border
items.note: Across from Myawaddy, open 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. Shop for Burmese souvenirs, jade, jewelry, dried goods, herbs and unusual snacks — it's Mae Sot's main shopping hub.

items.activity: Check in to your hotel in Mae Sot and relax
items.note: Sleep in Mae Sot the second night so you're set for nature the next morning. The town has an evening market and restaurants to stroll near your hotel.

blocks.title: About the Border
blocks.html: Walking the Thai side of Rim Moei market is easy, but if you want to cross into Myawaddy, always check the latest border situation and crossing rules first, since openings and closures change with the times. This trip is planned for the Thai side only, and that's plenty of fun on its own.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Nature Before You Head Home

items.activity: Drive from Mae Sot to Pha Charoen Waterfall
items.note: Inside Pha Charoen Waterfall National Park toward Phop Phra district. It's a limestone waterfall that tumbles down in many small tiers, an easy walk with a path that isn't steep.

items.activity: Soak in the natural hot springs near the waterfall
items.note: The springs run around 60°C — a relaxing foot soak before the long drive, a fitting rest stop before you head back.

items.activity: Lunch around Phop Phra or Mae Sot
items.note: Fuel up before driving back over the mountains. Eat your fill, because the return route is a long mountain stretch.

items.activity: Drive back over the mountains to Tak town
items.note: Allow about an hour and a half to two hours. You'll reach Tak town in the late afternoon, just in time for a ride home or another night if you're not rushing.

blocks.text: Rough Budget Per Person (Excluding Travel to Tak)

items: 2 nights' accommodation — mid-range hotels in Tak town/Mae Sot, around ฿600–1,200 per night
Food — ฿60–150 per meal per person, roughly ฿800–1,200 for the whole trip
Entry/park fees — Pha Charoen Waterfall has a national park fee; temples and Rim Moei market are free to walk
Fuel/car rental — depends on group size, and works out cheaper split among more people

blocks.title: Best Season
blocks.html: The waterfalls look best and run fullest in the late rainy to early cool season (October–January), with pleasantly cool weather that's ideal for the mountain drive. In the hot season the waterfalls can run low.

faq.q: Do I need my own car for a 3-day, 2-night Tak trip?
faq.a: Your own car or a rental is recommended, since the sights are spread across Tak town, Mae Sot and the waterfalls in Phop Phra district — they're far apart and public transport between them is limited. Driving yourself gives you more freedom to adjust your stops and timing.

faq.q: How far is it from Tak town to Mae Sot, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It's roughly 73–86 km along Highways 105/12, crossing the mountains past Doi Phawo, about an hour and a half of driving. It's a winding mountain road, so drive slowly and watch for trucks.

faq.q: Should I sleep in Tak town or Mae Sot?
faq.a: This plan suggests one night in Tak town first, then moving to Mae Sot for the second night, so you don't have to cross the mountains back and forth several times. It keeps the travel smooth and saves time.

faq.q: What time of year is best for visiting Tak?
faq.a: The late rainy to early cool season, around October to January, is best — the waterfalls run full and the cool weather is great for the mountain drive. In the hot season the waterfalls can run low and the weather is hotter.

faq.q: Can I cross into Myawaddy on the Myanmar side?
faq.a: You can freely walk and shop the Thai side of Rim Moei market. For crossing the checkpoint into Myawaddy, always check the latest border situation and crossing rules first, since openings and closures change with the times. This trip covers the Thai side only and is plenty of fun on its own.
